sources.title: Tokio spawn_blocking
sources.version_or_commit: Tokio 1.53.2; crate feature rt
sources.locator: Function description, cancellation and runtime shutdown sections
sources.observed_operation: A blocking closure uses a blocking pool with a high configured ceiling; started closures cannot be aborted, and shutdown may wait indefinitely.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Use only for bounded work that eventually finishes; unsuitable as the only containment mechanism for hostile/hung parsers.
sources.applicability: Tokio Rust apps using spawn_blocking; useful for bounded trusted blocking work, not forceful parser cancellation.

sources.title: Tokio CancellationToken
sources.version_or_commit: tokio-util 0.7.20 stable release; latest docs at capture
sources.observed_operation: cancel wakes waiting tasks and propagates to child tokens; cancellation itself is not atomic until return; the future is cancel-safe.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Cooperative async cancellation and job-scoped token hierarchy; does not terminate native/blocking code.
sources.applicability: Tokio async tasks and cooperative worker protocols; not an OS process kill.

sources.title: Tokio process Command
sources.version_or_commit: Tokio 1.53.2 stable release; latest docs at capture
sources.observed_operation: kill_on_drop defaults false; process_group is Unix-only; process tree and reaping require platform-specific handling.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Async child supervision; dropping a handle is not a portable process-tree kill.
sources.applicability: Rust/Tokio app-owned child renderers; process-group API is Unix-only and does not itself apply a sandbox.

sources.title: Rust std::process::Child
sources.version_or_commit: Rust standard-library APIs: kill stable since 1.0; try_wait since 1.18; live stable docs
sources.observed_operation: Child drop does not kill or wait; Unix force kill is SIGKILL; reaping is the caller's responsibility.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Direct-child primitive only; wait/reap explicitly, and add a platform process-group backend.
sources.applicability: Rust direct-child lifecycle on supported OSes; explicit kill/wait/reap is required.

sources.title: Tokio Semaphore
sources.version_or_commit: Tokio 1.53.2 stable release; latest docs at capture
sources.observed_operation: Permits are FIFO; acquire_many at the front can block a later smaller acquisition despite available permits.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Use as a running-work cap behind one priority dispatcher; avoid using FIFO permit arrival as class priority.
sources.applicability: Tokio execution-slot accounting; use behind an app-owned dispatcher, not as the priority queue.

sources.title: Windows Job Objects
sources.version_or_commit: Win32 docs updated 2025-07-14; Windows versions called out in article
sources.locator: Managing Processes in Jobs; Job Limits; tree management
sources.observed_operation: A job groups processes, can set working-set/time/CPU limits and terminate all associated processes; child inheritance has breakaway exceptions; nested jobs begin with Windows 8 / Server 2012.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Windows child-process control/resource enforcement. Job Objects are not by themselves a filesystem/network sandbox.
sources.applicability: Windows-only process grouping, accounting, limits, and termination; no filesystem/network sandbox guarantee.

sources.title: Linux Landlock
sources.version_or_commit: Current Linux kernel documentation; supported ABI/rights vary by running kernel
sources.locator: Unprivileged enforcement, filesystem access rights, restrict_self
sources.observed_operation: Unprivileged enforcement requires no_new_privs; rules limit handled operations; files opened before sandboxing are outside path restrictions.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Optional Linux per-process sandbox backend; probe runtime ABI and pass only required handles/paths.
sources.applicability: Linux kernels with required Landlock ABI/rights; runtime feature probing and no_new_privs are necessary for an unprivileged launch.

sources.title: Windows AppContainer
sources.version_or_commit: Win32 docs; AppContainer introduced in Windows 8
sources.observed_operation: Launcher creates a profile and chooses capabilities; no access outside granted resources by default; the API and OS version must be checked.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Windows sandbox possibility, separate from Job Object supervision; package/ACL/capability integration is an owner/platform decision.
sources.applicability: Windows AppContainer process sandbox where supported; launcher/profile/capability and ACL setup required.

sources.title: Apple App Sandbox inheritance and XPC
sources.version_or_commit: Archived Apple entitlement reference; code-signed App Sandbox targets
sources.observed_operation: A child process does not provide XPC's privilege-separation security; inherited child receives only static entitlements; post-launch file access must be passed as data or bookmark; XPC is preferred.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: macOS sandboxed packaging route, subject to signing/entitlement setup and file-access handoff.
sources.applicability: macOS sandboxed app packaging and helper design; archived guidance makes signing, entitlement, and selected-file handoff relevant.

sources.title: Apple Quick Look Thumbnailing
sources.version_or_commit: Current Apple API docs; availability is OS/platform dependent
sources.observed_operation: Supports async best and progressive representations and cancellation; format set varies by OS and installed thumbnail extensions.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Native adapter/fallback for Apple platforms; not a cross-platform scheduler or hostile-parser contract.
sources.applicability: Apple-platform native thumbnail adapter for supported formats; use only as optional platform behavior with its own cancellation/results.

sources.title: Windows Shell Thumbnail Handlers
sources.version_or_commit: Windows Shell documentation describing Vista-era API model; verify on target supported Windows releases
sources.locator: Thumbnail Processes; Thumbnail Cache and Sizing
sources.observed_operation: Handlers run out of process by default in documented model, but can opt out via registry; cache invalidation includes last-modified time; size buckets can change.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Potential OS fast path only; external handlers, registry and shell cache weaken deterministic app-level limits.
sources.applicability: Windows Shell integration only; depends on Shell registrations and registry isolation/cache settings.

sources.title: SQLite atomic commit
sources.version_or_commit: Current SQLite technical documentation; explicitly rollback-journal mode
sources.observed_operation: A transaction appears all-or-nothing across crash/power failure in rollback-journal mode; journal names must remain for recovery.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Possible persistent cache metadata store. If WAL mode is chosen, validate its separate semantics; previews remain rebuildable.
sources.applicability: Optional local persistent cache metadata using SQLite rollback-journal mode; not evidence for WAL without additional review.

sources.title: freedesktop Thumbnail Managing Standard
sources.version_or_commit: Version 0.9.0 (2020); XDG desktop standard
sources.locator: Thumbnail directory, Thumb::URI/MTime/Size, Detect Modifications and failure cache
sources.observed_operation: Per-user XDG cache; URI and second-resolution mtime; size should be checked; spec warns files may share same one-second mtime; failed-cache keys should be app/version-specific.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Useful cache precedent, but mtime/URI alone is not a strong content revision for this app.
sources.applicability: Linux/XDG desktop thumbnail interoperability precedent; not a strong content-validity key for a reference manager.

sources.title: Zotero 7 changelog
sources.version_or_commit: zotero-docs commit 0218554ffa63c2fd005f3167ccd4a92d64306866; includes 7.0.4 and 7.0.12 release history
sources.observed_operation: Version history records a disappearance fix in 7.0.4 and a wrong-item rapid-switching preview fix in 7.0.12.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Direct desktop attachment-preview regression history; evidence of race-sensitive visible results.
sources.applicability: Zotero 7 product release history for attachment-preview regression/fix chronology.

sources.title: Zotero attachmentPreview.js
sources.version_or_commit: Zotero v7.0.12 tag resolves to commit 6af5a484fd6688aab23150938d69df42dfca10e4
sources.observed_operation: Retains one latest task, serializes preview/discard work and rejects a completed render if selected item id changed; timeout race unblocks task bookkeeping.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: A close production precedent; item id equality alone omits edit revision/options and must not replace a stronger acceptance key.
sources.applicability: Zotero 7.0.12 attachment preview implementation; a concrete stale-item guard precedent, not a universal renderer contract.

sources.title: Zotero PDFWorker manager
sources.version_or_commit: Zotero v7.0.12 tag resolves to commit 6af5a484fd6688aab23150938d69df42dfca10e4
sources.observed_operation: One Web Worker processes a FIFO queue; priority uses unshift; error handler logs worker error but this file shows no restart.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Illustrates a worker protocol and serialization tradeoff; no OS process isolation and strict priority can delay ordinary jobs.
sources.applicability: Zotero 7.0.12 PDF Web Worker queue implementation; shows serialized processing and front insertion, not process supervision.

sources.title: Zotero document-worker
sources.observed_operation: Shared modules run in Node for tests/tooling; production emits Web Worker for Zotero desktop and reuses code in iOS JavaScriptCore.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Current renderer/worker architecture precedent; JavaScript Web Worker is not an OS process security boundary.
sources.applicability: Zotero document processing worker architecture across Node, desktop Web Worker, and iOS JSContext; not an OS security sandbox.

sources.title: ZoteroThumbFile 1.1.5
sources.version_or_commit: Release tag v1.1.5 resolves to commit 22a07714ae8227aa560921c4b4262eb47eb05bac; released 2026-09-25
sources.locator: README Rendering and limits / Compatibility; bootstrap.js and tests/plugin.test.cjs
sources.observed_operation: Two render tasks, 48-image and approximately 24 MiB image-string cache per reader, viewport-near loading, old raster retained until replacement decode; maintainer reports 13 tests and Zotero 10.0.4 macOS test.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Recent independent PDF contact-sheet implementation only; uses Zotero internals, tests are self-reported and were not run here.
sources.applicability: Independent Zotero PDF contact-sheet extension on Zotero 9/10; local implementation/testing precedent with private API/version limits.

sources.title: Apple OperationQueue and Operation cancellation
sources.version_or_commit: Current Apple Foundation docs; Apple platform APIs
sources.locator: Determine Execution Order; Respond to Operation Cancelation; QoS and maxConcurrentOperationCount
sources.observed_operation: Priority/readiness choose work; queued operations cannot be directly removed; cancellation must be cooperatively checked; default custom-queue QoS is background.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Native queue alternative on Apple only; illustrates limits of framework cancellation and strict queue control.
sources.applicability: Apple Foundation operation scheduling/cancellation only; useful conceptual alternative, not cross-platform semantics.

sources.title: Zotero preview feature issue
sources.version_or_commit: Zotero issue #238; opened 2013-01-31, closed 2025-02-14
sources.observed_operation: A preview-pane request remained open through years and was later reported added in Zotero 7.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Product history only; changelog/source are stronger evidence for actual later bug fixes.
sources.applicability: Zotero feature-request history for preview pane; use as product context, not proof of current implementation behavior.
